title: 'The art of thinking': illustrated statement hero with a design-history timeline footer
contains_third_party_content: Names of architects and designers appear as text (Adolf Loos, Marcel Breuer, Gerrit Rietveld, Alvar Aalto, Max Bill, Verner Panton, Jasper Morrison); the sneakers resemble real athletic shoe designs.

observed.layout: Full-bleed cornflower blue. Right half: a flat vector illustration of legs and sneakers on a skateboard whose deck is a yellow baguette, with a diagonal dark-blue shadow. Left: a huge, heavy geometric headline 'The art of thinking' in white. Tiny captions top-left, a rotated caption on the far left, a hamburger icon top-right. Bottom: six design-history entries (object, designer, year) on hairlines.
observed.hierarchy: Headline, then the illustration, then the caption row.
observed.typography: Heavy geometric display headline; tiny sans captions. Typeface unconfirmed.
observed.materials: Flat vector with a hard diagonal shadow.

interpretation.aesthetic: Playful modernist: three hues and a visual pun (bread plus skateboard) for 'thinking differently'.
implementation_notes: The illustration is a custom asset; layout is standard.
The shadow is a flat shape that directs the eye toward the headline.

concept_work.essence: A single idea (a pun) carried by one illustration, one huge headline and a calm structured counterweight.
what_makes_it_work: Blue against yellow gives a hard focal point.
The shadow diagonal pulls the eye to the headline.
The timeline footer balances the loud illustration.
gaps_to_make_it_work: The white headline on blue measures about 2.79:1.
The link between the pun and the design-history captions is unclear.
There is no offer or CTA; navigation is a hamburger only.

links: The shadow diagonal leads the eye toward the headline.
Timeline years progress left to right.

approach: Standard layout for headline and caption row

pattern.name: Illustrated statement hero
use_when: Brand or editorial pages where mood matters more than a transaction
adaptation_examples: Museum exhibition page: object illustration with a dated catalogue row.
Newsletter landing: pun illustration and issue list.

lessons: Large display text still needs contrast: white on mid-blue falls just under 3:1.
A pun needs one extra layer of meaning for the brand.

measured.palette_method: Median-cut quantization of the supplied image plus saturated-pixel hue medians. Approximate (JPEG). Items marked 'approx' were judged by eye.
measured.color_roles: One cornflower-blue field, a yellow object as the single complement, pink and navy for the figure and shadow, white type.
measured.contrast_method: Estimated from compressed images. Background = dominant color in a box around the text. ratio_low = conservative estimate (mean of the most distant ~4% of pixels). ratio = best estimate (mean of the most distant ~1.5% of pixels; for text on a saturated background that appears near-white or near-black, the text is assumed pure white or black, because anti-aliasing of small text otherwise understates the contrast). Accessibility scores use ratio_low; critical failure CF1 uses ratio. Gradient or photo backgrounds are measured one text line at a time. Values within 0.4 of a threshold are borderline and should be verified in the source file.

evidence: Mood is clear but there is no offer or action, so purpose is only partly readable.
Strong focal point, scale contrast and restrained palette.
Editorial conventions are met, but a hamburger-only navigation and no CTA leave the page without an action path.
No states, no CTA, hamburger-only menu.
Consistent hue, type and hairline treatment.
A visual pun carried through illustration and layout is distinctive.
Scored on conservative values: primary text min 2.79:1; secondary text min 2.79:1; icon min n/a:1; non-color state cue: True.
accessibility.basis: computed from measured contrast + cue flag (scope: contrast and non-color cues only; touch targets, motion and screen-reader support cannot be assessed from a static image)

critical_failures.description: A primary text/label measures below 3:1 contrast (best estimate)

evaluation.readiness_key: A = ship with minor adjustments (>=80, no critical failure); B = needs specific fixes (60-79); C = rethink (<60)
evaluation.scope: Scored as presented in a static image. States, motion and behavior that are not shown are not scored as present.
